text.p: Xerox Corp. said Thursday that net income grew by 15 percent in the second quarter, but revenue growth was slight because sales from its new digital products have not yet started to kick in.
Xerox also said earnings and revenues were hurt by the adverse effect of currency, due to the strengthening dollar, which it said will become even greater in the second half.
The giant maker of copiers and other office products said its net income for the three months ended June 30 rose to $337 million, or 94 cents a share, up from from $293 million, or 81 cents a share.

The company said the 1997 income included $13 million, or 4 cents a share, realized from its acquisition last month of the remaining interest in Rank Xerox -- which manufactures, markets and services Xerox products in Europe, parts of Asia and Africa -- from Britain's Rank Group Plc.

The earnings per share, before the 4-cent gain, were one penny ahead of Wall Street expectations of 89 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates. Xerox expects to see more gains from Rank in the second half.

"Basically it looked like the numbers were pretty much in line with estimates," said Peter Enderlin, a Smith Barney analyst. "Certainly, currency was a factor. They indicated it would be worse for the rest of the year."
Xerox said that in the second half of 1997 it expects to see a negative impact due to currency ranging from a bit more than 10 cents a share to a bit less than 20 cents a share.
Xerox, based in Stamford, Conn., said revenues grew by 3 percent to $4.4 billion from $4.2 billion.
However, excluding the impact of currency translations, Xerox said, revenue expanded by 6 percent, driven by strong growth in equipment sales and document outsourcing.

Xerox said sales of its digital products grew 24 percent in the quarter, driven by excellent growth in color copiers and printers and strong growth in high-speed laser printers. Analysts expect digital revenues to increase in the second half, as just-introduced products begin to ship in volume.

"Revenues would have been a lot stronger, but they announced all these products coming in September and December...and I think they ended up with a huge backlog," said Alex Henderson, a Prudential Securities analyst.

Xerox said production publishing revenues showed good growth, despite some slowdown due to new product anticipation. Customers delayed purchases during the period in expectation of a new 180-page-per minute DocuTech Production Publisher, which is now widely available.

The DocuColor 40, its 40-page-per-minute color document processing system, continued to contribute significantly to revenue growth, it said. Xerox said that it has had "excellent customer acceptance" of the products it introduced in April and May, and that orders for its black-and-white digital copiers have been double its expectations.

"We will certainly see a big surge in the digital products that were launched in the first half of the year, which hardly registered in the first half," said Barry Romeril, chief financial officer, in a phone interview. He declined to be more specific but said that sales from digital products will help the company meet its goal of 10 percent revenue growth "is foreseeable in the next few quarters."
Digital product revenues represented 34 percent of total second-quarter revenues and represent the major growth area for Xerox, as its older, light lens business slowly drops off.
Black and white light lens copier sales dropped 3 percent in the quarter, Xerox said, reflecting pricing pressures and the impact of customers moving to digital technology.

Xerox is still developing light lens products, as it seeks to gain an even greater market share and it also introduced new light lens products during the quarter. Light lens products now account for 52 percent of total revenues.

The company said that as a result of its focus on productivity and expense controls, the ratio of selling, administrative and general expenses to revenues improved by a half percentage point to 29.6 percent.
Xerox stock closed down $1.56 at $78.44 in composite New York Stock Exchange trading.
